game.intro: Mud season just signed a treaty with the boot rack, and Saturn demands a front page. Fill the blank. Hold the presses.
game.headline: MUD BOOTS SIGN PEACE TREATY WITH FRONT HALL, ___ REFUSES TO ATTEND

game.intro: The peepers are back, singing in the ditches like a tiny swamp choir. Saturn wants accompaniment. Count the keys.
game.question: A standard 88-key piano has black keys and white keys. How many of the keys are white?
game.source: Standard 88-key piano: 52 white keys + 36 black keys = 88 (7 full octaves of 7 white keys = 49, plus A0, B0 and C8)

game.intro: The moon just moved into Joel's sign and kicked its boots off at the cabin door. Ten seconds a pair. Go.
DES alert: two blue umbrellas, one sidewalk. Saturn wants to know if your brains match as well as your gear.
game.question: You open an umbrella you forgot you owned and something falls out. What do you hope it is?
options: A note in your own handwriting
A key to nothing you own

game.intro: New moon, fresh start, tiny seeds. Saturn wants to see something small with big ambitions.
game.prompt: Something in your home smaller than a seed packet that has a very big job. Get close enough that it looks important.

game.intro: Darkest sky of May. Perfect lighting for being confidently, magnificently wrong.
game.question: Where does the sun go at night?

game.intro: Gemini moon means two of everything, including noise. Especially noise.
game.prompt: Two sounds from a busy kitchen happening at the same time, performed solo. The other guesses both.

game.intro: A thin crescent smile is back in the sky. Saturn asks you to smile back, in pictures only.
game.prompt: Something that always makes you grin within three seconds.

game.intro: Windows open, house breathing again. Tell the truth twice and let one fib drift in on the breeze.
game.prompt: Three sounds that came through your window this week. One never happened.

game.intro: First day on the clothesline. Hang your answers out fast, the wind is not waiting.
Half a moon, full nerve. Pick bravely, then guess what the other one was brave enough to pick.
game.question: Which tiny act of courage would you rather do today?
options: Ask a stranger their dog's name
Send a voice memo, no retakes

game.intro: Don't even scream: two lion shirts, one room. The moon is in Leo and it wants its close-up.
game.prompt: Something with a mane, a fringe or tassels. Get so close it looks like a jungle.

game.intro: Someone borrowed the crown and Saturn has questions. Answer wrongly, but with royal confidence.
game.question: What are royal crowns traditionally made of?

game.intro: Virgo moon, spreadsheet energy. Saturn wants to hear things getting sorted.
game.prompt: Something being put neatly in its place: a drawer closing, a stapler landing, a very satisfied filing cabinet.

game.intro: The lilac buds have been watching all week. Nobody knows what they saw. You decide.
game.headline: LILAC BUDS CAUGHT ___ ON BACKYARD CAMERA, NEIGHBOURHOOD DEMANDS ANSWERS

game.intro: Libra moon, balanced stones, everything in neat rows. Stack your guess carefully and do not topple past the top.
game.question: A classic 9-by-9 number-placement puzzle grid, the kind with nine 3-by-3 boxes, has how many little squares?

game.intro: First porch evening of the year. Answer fast so you can get back to doing nothing beautifully.
Full Moon Recharge night. Ruby and onyx side by side on the sill. Now line your minds up too.
game.question: The full moon offers to take one chore off your plate for a whole week. What do you hand it?

game.intro: DES: a dog in yellow rain boots. Saturn rules that today's photos must be equally ridiculous.
game.prompt: Something yellow. Zoom in until it looks like the surface of a mystery planet.

game.intro: Fullest moon of spring, and Saturn is wearing a party hat. Celebrate by being spectacularly incorrect.
game.question: What makes the moon look full?

game.intro: Long weekend launch sequence initiated. Saturn needs the soundtrack.
game.prompt: A long weekend starting, in one noise. Car door, screen door, a giant sigh of relief: your call.

game.intro: Your hoodie smells like a campfire and Saturn approves. Tell the whole story in pictures.
game.prompt: Your perfect campfire evening, from the first spark to the last ember.

game.intro: The moon is climbing Nancy's mountain. Carry three tales up the trail and hide one fib in the backpack.
game.prompt: Three places you have stood that had a great view. One is pure fiction.

game.intro: Planting day. Ten seconds a pair, which Saturn insists is how long a seed takes to sprout.
Aquarius moon, inventor energy. Pick the gadget you'd build, then guess what the other one built.
game.question: Which ridiculous invention would you actually use every day?

game.intro: The cosmic broom is out, sweeping the sky tidy. Show us what it missed.
game.prompt: Something with bristles: a brush, a broom, a doormat, a very fluffy cat. Get close enough to count them.

game.intro: DES: you both took the same lilac photo. Prove you don't share one brain by being wrong differently.
game.question: What colour are lilacs?

game.intro: The fog rolled in and swallowed the harbour. Saturn wants to hear it from inside the soup.
game.prompt: A foghorn, a buoy bell or a gull lost in the mist. Pick one and give it everything.

game.intro: Beach glass season. Somewhere a little green shard is about to be very famous.
game.headline: BEACHCOMBER FINDS SEA GLASS SHAPED EXACTLY LIKE ___, EXPERTS BAFFLED

game.intro: The moon swings back into Joel's sign for a return visit and plants a flag. Saturn wants to know how pointy it is.
game.question: How many points does the red maple leaf on Canada's national flag have?
game.source: The stylized maple leaf on the Canadian flag (proclaimed 1965) has 11 points

game.intro: Last night of May. Wave goodbye to spring with three snap decisions.
